source_pages: printed p.245-247 / PDF 247-249, read whole and verified against 170-dpi renders 2026-08-23
family_naming_note: Namespaced 'Wall H.96' for the same reason as every other wall family.
extraction_note: Eight of eleven positions, 23 of 27 codes. LEFT OUT: the 90-degree corner (OF0723 / OF0725), the corner wall unit (PF094D/S) - both Elda Q7b - and PF0696, which is 600 tall and lives in wall_h96_microwave_niche.json under family Wall H.60.
letter_note: PF = H.96 was named by the filler table on printed p.434 (PF0151) and confirmed by a sweep of printed p.245-247. F is H.96 and G is H.84: the letters run BACKWARDS across that pair, which is why they are a lookup and never a sequence.

data.mounting_note: Catalog-level fact: every unit in the wall chapter hangs. HOW HIGH is a project decision and lives in Standards::WALL_MOUNT_BOTTOM_MM until M1.6.
page_observations: THE STACK IS EQUAL AGAIN - 48 ON TOP, 48 BELOW - AND THE PLURAL WORDING COMES BACK WITH IT. H.72 splits 36 + 36 and prints '2 top-hung doors'; H.84 splits 48 + 36 and prints '1 top-hung door' twice, on separate lines; H.96 splits 48 + 48 and prints '2 top-hung doors' again. THREE families now, and the wording tracks the geometry every time. That is no longer a guess about this catalog's habits - but it is still read off the page and never used to derive a split, because both figures are dimensioned on every elevation.

THE MICROWAVE-NICHE POSITION CHANGES ITS DOOR. PE0696 (H.72) and PG0696 (H.84) are headed 'Wall unit with top-hung door'; PF0696 is headed 'Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door' and is HANDED, hinged on a vertical edge. Only the niche is constant across the three; the door is not. Anything that treated 'microwave niche' as one shape would be wrong here.

AND IT IS THE SECTION HEIGHT MINUS 360 FOR THE THIRD TIME - 960 - 360 = 600, after 720 - 360 = 360 and 840 - 360 = 480. The H.84 file said the third instance would decide whether this is a rule. IT IS DECIDED AND THE ANSWER IS NO: it stays an observation and derives nothing, because every one of the three PRINTS its own elevation. A derivation that can only ever agree with a printed number buys nothing and costs the day a family prints something else.

THE FOLDING TYPE STOPS AT W.90, as at H.84 - but its compound has TWO codes here (105, 120) where H.84 has THREE (105, 120, 180). The 180 is gone and so is the finish restriction that hung on it: this compound carries none at all.
THE CORNER SUFFIX MOVES. The 90-degree corner is OF0723 / OF0725 here against OG0713 / OG0715 at H.84. Both are gated, and the digit pair is recorded so nobody builds a corner code by analogy.
The two boiler housings are d.62, exactly as at H.72 and H.84. Three families agreeing now.
The one-door type keeps the 2 shelves H.84 introduced.

wall_pull_out_door.description: Wall unit with pull-out door - 1 door - 1 soft-close pull-out door - no Push-pull device
wall_pull_out_door.notes: One W.15 code, suffix 30, as at H.72 and H.84.

front_layout.note: One full-height front on a pull-out mechanism. NO hinge_axis and no open_leaf - the travel is not in the catalog.

wall_door.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door - 2 shelves
wall_door.notes: Four widths, the same set as H.72 and H.84, and the same two shelves as H.84. ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order.

wall_two_doors.description: Wall unit with doors - 2 doors - 2 shelves
wall_two_doors.notes: Two widths, as at H.72 and H.84.

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle.

wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.description: Wall unit with top-hung doors - 2 top-hung doors - 2 shelves - top door with Push-pull device
wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.notes: TWO EQUAL LEAVES - 480 above 480, both dimensioned on the elevation and summing to 960 - and the page goes back to the plural '2 top-hung doors' that H.84's unequal pair gave up. Only the TOP door carries a Push-pull device. Suffix 04, which is a side-by-side compound at H.48 and H.60 and a stacked pair here, at H.72 and at H.84.

front_layout.note: 480 then 480, summing to the family's 960. NO hinge_axis: one key cannot carry two leaves. Slabs are correct - two of them, which is also the handle count.

wall_folding_doors.description: Wall unit with horizontally folding doors - 2 doors - 2 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_folding_doors.notes: Four widths, stopping at 90 as at H.84. Suffix 89 in all three families. The page prints '2 doors' on one line here, where H.84 prints '1 door' twice - the same wording shift the top-hung position makes, and for the same reason: the leaves are equal again.

front_layout.note: 480 then 480. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism figure - a folding pair moves in a way this catalog has not dimensioned.

wall_compound_2_folding.description: Wall unit with horizontally folding doors - 2 doors - 4 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_compound_2_folding.notes: TWO codes where H.84 has three - there is no 1800 here. NO finish_restrictions block: the render prints no prohibition symbol on this position, where H.84's carries one. The word 'Compound' appears nowhere; the module splits are what identify it. Four shelves against the simple type's two, one pair per module.

wall_boiler_housing_door.description: Wall boiler housing - 1 rh/lh door - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_door.notes: d.62, same widths and same suffix 01 as its H.72 and H.84 twins.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order.

wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.description: Wall boiler housing - 2 doors - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.notes: Suffix 00 is a boiler housing in the third family running - and the three families that use those digits that way are the three that have boiler housings at all.

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle.
